_note: The [I] tier. Names, record fields and globals that a filter, a caller or a
neighbouring name produced and that nothing has yet checked. They are NOT symbols.
Nothing here is applied to Ghidra and nothing here may be cited as a finding.
docs/symbols.json is the verified tier and its ratio is deliberately high: a name
moves there only once someone has run a check that COULD have failed and it did
not, with that check written into its comment. This file exists so that leads can
be written down in bulk without diluting that. Promotion is one direction only,
and a refuted entry is DELETED rather than softened. Correction C3 in
docs/decisions.md is what a coherent, unchecked model costs when it is filed as
fact.
Every entry carries a basis: the mechanical observation the guess rests on - an
L2.eng group and index, a widget-table membership, a shipped filename, a caller.
An entry whose basis is only "it is called from near something named" is the
shape C3 took and should be read as a question, not an answer.
The rate to expect is measured in docs/method.md section 7.3: the subject filter
runs 89% correct and the role hypothesis on top of it 58%. So roughly two in five
of the roles below are wrong, and the value of this file is that it says which two
in five to check first - not that it is right.
SCHEMA NOTE - the confidence key currently holds two different things, because
two agents created this file independently on the same day and each read the spec
a different way. Both forms are kept verbatim rather than one being rewritten into
the other, which would be an integrator inventing data:
an enum - subject | role | both - saying WHICH HALF of the name is the guess.
subject: what the function is about is anchored to a string or an asset,
and the role word may be wrong.
role:    the role is anchored (it is in a widget table, it is a painter)
and the subject is the guess.
both:    neither half has an independent anchor. Read this before using it.
a prose line saying what would have to be true and what would refute it.
The two are not interchangeable: the enum is countable against the measured
rates above, the prose is not. Unifying them is a decision for whoever owns this
file, not for the merge that first put them side by side.
See docs/method.md section 7.6.

functions.name: Ui_DispatchPointer
functions.basis: 8,140 bytes, the largest unnamed function in the interface. Its opening is Screen_HitRegion, then Screen_HandleInput, then a per-screen fallback chain that on the campaign map tries Map_EdgeScroll, Menu_OpenDropdown(g_menuBarItems, 3), CountyStrip_Click, CountyStrip_JobClick and Map_Click in that order. It writes g_screenId with 30 different values - more than any other function in the binary.
functions.comment: The top-level pointer dispatcher: one click, routed to whatever the current screen wants. Only the first 6% of the body has been read; the name claims the role, not the whole behaviour.

functions.name: SaveLoad_Accept
functions.basis: Record 0 of g_saveLoadWidgets (0x004DDD78), frame 29 at (304, 64) - the tick of the tick/cross pair whose cross is the verified SaveLoad_Cancel. Its whole body is DAT_005CD41C = 100.
functions.comment: The save/load box's confirm button. What the sentinel 100 means to its reader has not been traced.

functions.name: Screen_MapInfo
functions.basis: The painter Screen_Draw dispatches for g_screenId 0x04, which FUN_0042FF10 sets after a map click that picked something. Branches to UnitPanel_Draw when a unit is picked and FUN_0041BEFE otherwise, on the same g_pickedTileFlags bits Map_Click uses.
functions.comment: docs/screens-county.md calls this 'the map information panel'; nothing has read what it draws.

functions.name: Merchant_DrawPanel
functions.basis: The widget-pass companion Screen_DrawWidgets calls for screen 0x08, immediately before Widget_Draw on the merchant's own table.
functions.comment: The merchant screen's per-frame overlay. Subject is anchored by the screen id; what it draws is unread.

functions.name: Merchant_HandleInput
functions.basis: The input-pass companion Screen_HandleInput calls for screen 0x08, before Widget_Test on the merchant's table.
functions.comment: The merchant screen's non-widget hit-testing.

functions.name: Armoury_DrawPanel
functions.basis: Called by Screen_DrawWidgets for both armoury screens, 0x0A and 0x0D.
functions.comment: Shared overlay for the armoury and the armoury's buy list.

functions.name: Armoury_HandleInput
functions.basis: Called by Screen_HandleInput for screens 0x0A and 0x0D, before Hotspot_Test on a 9-entry table at 0x004DC938.
functions.comment: Shared input for the armoury screens.

functions.name: SendSupplies_DrawPanel
functions.basis: Called by Screen_DrawWidgets for screen 0x18, whose painter Screen_SendSupplies draws L2.eng group 33, 'Send supplies'.
functions.comment: The send-supplies overlay.

functions.name: SendSupplies_Close
functions.basis: Records 0 and 1 of the send-supplies widget table 0x004DD538: frames 29 and 31 at (320, 342) and (360, 346), hotspot ids 1 and 0 - the tick/cross convention. It writes g_screenId twice.
functions.comment: Accept or cancel the supply shipment; the hotspot id says which.

functions.name: SendSupplies_Less
functions.basis: Records 2 and 4 of the same table, frame 27 at x 216, hotspot ids 0 and 2 - two rows of a pair whose other half is 0x0043B27A at frame 25.
functions.comment: Decrease the amount of one commodity.

functions.name: SendSupplies_More
functions.basis: Records 3 and 5 of the same table, frame 25 at x 296, hotspot ids 0 and 2.
functions.comment: Increase the amount of one commodity.

functions.name: CastleBuild_Close
functions.basis: Both records of the castle-build widget table 0x004DDB80, frames 29 and 31 at (432, 440) and (472, 444), hotspot ids 1 and 0. It writes g_screenId five times.
functions.comment: Accept or abandon the castle design, on the verified Screen_CastleBuild.

functions.name: Armoury_BuyLess
functions.basis: Record 0 of the armoury buy table 0x004DD8C8, frame 68 at (176, 44); the four buttons in that row are frames 68, 66, 58 and 60, and 68/66 is the minus/plus pair the diplomacy gift row also uses.
functions.comment: One of the armoury buy-list's four buttons; the pairing is the evidence, not the body.

functions.name: Armoury_BuyMore
functions.basis: Record 1 of 0x004DD8C8, frame 66 at (208, 44).
functions.comment: The other half of the minus/plus pair.

functions.name: Armoury_BuyPrev
functions.basis: Record 2 of 0x004DD8C8, frame 58 at (240, 44). Frames 58 and 60 have not been identified in the button sheet.
functions.comment: Unanchored: only its position in the table is known.

functions.name: Armoury_BuyNext
functions.basis: Record 3 of 0x004DD8C8, frame 60 at (272, 44).
functions.comment: Unanchored: only its position in the table is known.

functions.name: SiegePrep_Add
functions.basis: Records 0, 2 and 4 of the siege-preparation widget table 0x004DDF10, frame 21 at x 38 and y 184 / 252 / 320, hotspot ids 0, 1 and 2. Screen_SiegePrep draws L2.eng group 83, whose indices 1, 2 and 3 are Catapults, Siege towers and Battering rams in that order. The body caps the count at 4, 4 and 2 respectively and refuses in a network game.
functions.comment: Order one more siege engine of the row's type. The caps 4 / 4 / 2 are read off the body and are not yet cross-checked against play.

functions.name: SiegePrep_Remove
functions.basis: Records 1, 3 and 5 of 0x004DDF10, frame 23, each 26 pixels below its partner, same hotspot ids. Decrements the same field while it is above zero.
functions.comment: Cancel one ordered siege engine.

functions.name: Diplo_AdjustGift
functions.basis: Records 6 and 7 of g_diploWidgets, frames 68 and 66 at (184, 240) and (216, 240), hotspot ids 1 and 0 - the minus/plus pair. The screen it sits on draws L2.eng group 72 index 18, 'Gift of', beside g_diploGold.
functions.comment: Raise or lower the offered gift; the hotspot id says which way.

functions.name: SmackTest_Step
functions.basis: Records 0 and 1 of the screen 0x44 widget table 0x004DDFA0, frames 68 and 66 at (208, 232) and (240, 232). Screen 0x44's painter draws L2.eng group 89, whose index 0 is 'Smack file testing'.
functions.comment: Pick the previous or next Smacker file on the developers' test screen.

functions.name: SmackTest_Close
functions.basis: Records 2 and 3 of 0x004DDFA0, frames 29 and 31 - the tick/cross pair. It writes g_screenId.
functions.comment: Leave the Smacker test screen.

functions.name: Ratings_DrawPanel
functions.basis: Called by Screen_DrawWidgets for both 0x2E and 0x2F, the two Battle Master screens, and by Menu_NewGame before it opens its confirmation box.
functions.comment: Shared overlay for the two score screens. Being called from Menu_NewGame as well means the role may be wider than 'the ratings panel' - read it before promoting.

functions.name: Merchant_SeasonTick
functions.basis: Position in Season_Advance's call list, between County_RecountMerchants and Army_RecountCountyTroops, and its address - it sits between Merchant_AdvanceAll (0x004280E9) and Merchant_ResetStall (0x0042847C) in the merchant neighbourhood.
functions.confidence: The body is eleven bytes and returns. So the name is a guess at what was removed, and it cannot be checked from this binary at all: an empty function has no evidence in it. Recorded because a reader of Season_Advance needs to know the slot is deliberately empty rather than missing, not because the name is worth anything.
functions.comment: A season pass that does nothing. Called only from Season_Advance.

functions.name: Army_ProcessPendingDisbands
functions.basis: First call in Wages_PayAll, ahead of Army_Starve. Walks every kind-1 unit, calls FUN_004ABA5A on it, and destroys any whose county byte is above 16.
functions.confidence: The stray-army half is directly readable and near-certain; the disband half rests on FUN_004ABA5A, which returns an army's men to its home county's population when unit +0x167 is 1 and clears the flag when it is more - so +0x167 looks like a disband request with a one-season delay, and that reading is unchecked. Cross-subsystem: this belongs to whoever owns armies, not to the season pipeline. Refuted if +0x167 turns out to be set anywhere other than a disband order.
functions.comment: Retires armies at the top of the wage pass: honours pending disbands, then destroys any army standing outside every county.

functions.name: Army_DisbandPending
functions.basis: Sole caller is FUN_004AD39A. Reads unit +0x167: at 1 it adds menTotal back to the home county's population and popArmy and destroys the unit; above 1 it decrements the flag to 0 instead.
functions.confidence: The effect is plain; what is not established is what sets +0x167, and therefore whether this is a disband order, a garrison return, or something else. Find the writer of +0x167 and this either promotes or dies.
functions.comment: Returns an army's men to its home county and destroys it, when unit +0x167 says one is pending.

fields.name: merchantFlag
fields.basis: County_RecountMerchants zeroes it alongside +0x1A4 and +0x1A5, the two merchant fields.
fields.confidence: Zero in every county of every fixture, and nothing else in the corpus writes it, so the zeroing is all the evidence there is. It sits immediately before rationAchieved (+0x15D), so a width error here would be visible; it is a byte. Refuted if a writer turns up outside the merchant code.

fields.name: fieldsOther
fields.basis: County_RecountFields buckets tile graphics 0, 23 and 24 here, next to the three named field tallies.
fields.confidence: Zero in all fourteen counties of the England fixture, so the reproduction that verified the other four tallies could not verify this one - a bucket that never fires is a bucket whose meaning is unknown. Graphic 0 is an empty slot; 23 and 24 are not identified. Needs a save with those tiles.

fields.name: fieldsReclaimable
fields.basis: County_RecountFields buckets tile graphic 25 and above here; Field_SetType switches the reclamation labour share on exactly when it is non-zero.
fields.confidence: The gate in Field_SetType is direct and strong - this counts land the county can reclaim. What is not checked is the graphic band: it is 0 in every fixture, so no save demonstrates which tiles land in it. Promote when a save with wasteland exists.

fields.name: farmStyle
fields.basis: Ai_ManageCountyFarms writes it from g_aiPersonality's farmStyle and immediately dispatches on 0, 1 and 9.
fields.confidence: Strong: the fixture holds only 0, 1 and 9, exactly the dispatched values. Left here rather than promoted because unowned counties also carry 1, and Ai_ManageCountyFarms only writes AI-owned ones, so something at map load writes it too and has not been found. The name may be too narrow.

fields.name: purse
fields.basis: Merchant_Trade credits and debits it instead of realm gold when the realm argument is 0.
fields.confidence: Readable but never exercised: 0 in every fixture, because no unowned county has traded. The claim that an unowned county has a treasury of its own is a real one and it is untested.

fields.name: armyFoodForagers
fields.basis: Ration_Apply adds +0x198 + +0x19C to the county's food requirement when g_optArmiesEat is on, and Panel_Ration draws that same sum against L2.eng 87/8 'men foraging in the county.'. The orphaned ration group 62 has 'Soldiers', 'Foragers', 'take' and 'steal' as four separate strings, which is where the split into two fields comes from.
fields.confidence: That the pair exists and sums into the food bill is certain. Which of the two is soldiers and which is foragers is a guess off the dead string group, and is a coin flip. Both are 0 in every fixture - no fixture has an army standing in a county with Armies Eat on.

fields.name: receivedTotal
fields.basis: Merchant_Trade adds the crown amount to +0x104 and +0x108 on a purchase and to +0x10C and +0x110 on a sale.
fields.confidence: That two accumulators run on spending and two on income is certain. Which of each pair is the season figure and which the running total is not: nothing in the corpus resets either, and all four are 0 in every fixture because no fixture has traded. If neither is ever reset, the pair is something else entirely - two panels rather than two horizons.

globals.name: g_screenIdSaved
globals.basis: Written with the current g_screenId by Menu_LoadGame, Menu_SaveGame and Ui_OpenConfirm, and read back into g_screenId by SaveLoad_Cancel. Sixteen other functions touch it.
globals.comment: The screen a modal box returns to. Distinct from g_menuPrevScreen, which the menu-bar drop-down uses; why there are two has not been established.

globals.name: g_fileListTop
globals.basis: The only value SaveLoad_Scroll moves, by the widget's hotspot id, clamped at 0 and against DAT_004EB25C with a window of 15 rows for list 1 and 5 for list 2.
globals.comment: First visible row of the save/load file list.

globals.name: g_fileListCount
globals.basis: The bound SaveLoad_Scroll clamps g_fileListTop against.
globals.comment: How many files the save/load list holds.

globals.name: g_siegeArmy
globals.basis: The index SiegePrep_Add and SiegePrep_Remove multiply by 0x1A4 to reach the record holding the three siege-engine counts at +0x232 relative to 0x0052F000, six bytes apart.
globals.comment: Which army the siege-preparation screen is ordering engines for. The 0x1A4 stride has not been matched to a named record type.

globals.name: g_playerSlots
globals.basis: Mp_DropDepartedPlayers tests slot +0x00 for zero; Realm_Eliminate clears +0x00, +0x25, +0x26 and sets +0x27. Stride 0x2C, six entries, one per realm.
globals.confidence: A per-realm table whose first word means 'this realm is still attached' is the only reading that makes both functions work. What the table actually holds - a network peer, a save slot, a controller - is not established, and the name presumes the first.

globals.name: g_playerCount
globals.basis: Decremented by Mp_DropDepartedPlayers each time a realm is dropped.
globals.confidence: One writer, one direction. Nothing here shows what increments it or who reads it.

globals.name: g_tradeGood
globals.basis: Indexes g_merchantStall in the trade panel and selects the branch in the good-to-stock switch.
globals.confidence: Consistent everywhere it appears. Not promoted because the trade screen was not read end to end here - only the transaction underneath it.

globals.name: g_startForcesSetting
globals.basis: Indexes g_startArmoury (stride 0x18) and, alongside g_startTroops's own index, seeds a new game's armoury.
globals.confidence: Both tables have exactly four meaningful rows, so the setting takes four values, which matches a new-game option. Which option, and whether 0..3 runs weakest to strongest, is inferred from the rows being monotonic and nothing else.
